Hi all — long answer below but TL;DR recommendation at top.

TL;DR recommended pilot mix
- H100 (80GB+ HBM3) — 4 GPUs dedicated to Llama-2-70b endpoints (primary low-latency path)
- A100 80GB — 6 GPUs for Llama-2-13b & fallbacks (better cost/availability tradeoff than 40GB in our testing)
- L4 (48GB GDDR) — 3 GPUs for embeddings and cost-sensitive lightweight routes; use batching heavily

Rationale / tradeoffs
- H100: best raw throughput and FP8 options. 70B is memory-hungry; full-precision KV + context favor H100 80/96GB HBM3. H100 gives ~1.8-2.5x perf vs A100 80GB on long sequences in our internal benchmarks; it also reduces sharding complexity (fewer nodes for the same model). Downsides: procurement lead time and higher unit cost.

- A100: well-understood, widely available, good for 13B and mid-sized models. 80GB A100 offers a good balance; 40GB variants force more aggressive tensor/model parallelism which increases latency for small requests. For predictable p95 <100ms on 13B models, 80GB A100s are preferable.

- L4: very cost-effective for embeddings and static/short-context models. Can't host 70B, but for embeddings it's perfect if you take advantage of batching and quantized kernels. Good candidate for autoscaled worker pools and burst capacity.

Quantization and perf knobs
- 70B: recommend FP8 or int8+kv-cache where feasible; we can reduce memory to fit into H100 with 1-2 shards and still meet latency targets. Must validate quality on our eval set — quantization regresses generation quality for some prompts.
- 13B: int8 / int4 works well, expect ~1.8-2.2x token throughput improvements with negligible quality loss for most QA/completion tasks.

Estimated capacity (conservative) — expected sustained throughput per GPU (approx):
- H100 (70B): ~30-40 concurrent small-chat QPS per GPU at p95<100ms (depends on prompt length & batch). With 4 GPUs we get ~120-160 concurrent capacity.
- A100 80GB (13B): ~60-80 concurrent small-chat QPS per GPU; 6 GPUs -> ~360-480 capacity.
- L4 (embeddings): ~2000 batched QPS across 3 GPUs if batching windows are well tuned (batch size 256-1024 depending on latency).

Cost/ops notes
- Rough monthly committed costs (ballpark) per GPU type (reserved pricing estimates): H100: $9k-$12k / GPU / month; A100 80GB: $4.5k-$7k / GPU / month; L4: $1.2k-$2k / GPU / month. These are region and vendor dependent — include 15% margin for networking/infra.

Risks & mitigations
- Procurement lead time for H100: propose a staged approach — start pilot with mixed A100 + L4 and a small H100 allocation (or use hosted H100 for the first 2–4 weeks) while reserved H100 is provisioned.
- Quantization quality regressions: lock a small eval set, run A/B compare (we can run on Redwood Optimize).
- Autoscaling and cold-starts: use a small warm standby pool and prefix/KV cache to hide rewarm penalties.

Attachments: I attached a short capacity spreadsheet with node counts (capacity_plan_v1.xlsx) and a draft SOW for procurement (SOW_draft_REDWOOD.pdf).

Next steps suggestion
1) Marcus: send this high-level to Oliver and ask for a 30–45 min alignment call (walk the spreadsheet).
2) Oliver: confirm acceptance criteria for quality (eval prompts) and procurement constraints.
3) We (SE + Sales): run a short quantization QA (1 week) against Oliver's eval prompts.

Happy to sync with a quick screen-share and walk the numbers.
